newsitem.title: UK: 1997 Who's Who shows who's 'in' and who's 'out'. [CORRECTED 19:07 GMT]
newsitem.headline: 1997 Who's Who shows who's 'in' and who's 'out'. [CORRECTED 19:07 GMT]

text.p: (Corrects by deleting erroneous reference to pop group Oasis. Only Oasis's Noel and Liam Gallagher are listed and have been since 1996).
Golfing sensation Tiger Woods made the latest International Who's Who but Prince Charles's mistress was left out.
Nine hundred men and women judged to have made their mark in politics, entertainment and sport have been added to the 61st edition out next week.
New entries this year include England's soccer captain Alan Shearer, Spanish flamenco dancer and sex symbol Joaquin Cortes and Canadian singer Alanis Morissette.
Bangladesh Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina Wajed and South Korean leader Kun Koh head a selection of politicians to win entries by making the headlines this year.

"People are chosen for their international significance - like presidents, prime ministers or Nobel prize winners - or for their achievement in a particular field or for their national importance," said Richard Fitzwilliams, editor for the past 22 years of the 20,000-long list of biographies.
Fitzwilliams said over the years his researchers had selected more and more names from the media and music industries to keep abreast with current trends.
"We've seen the music industry achieve tremendous importance and the influence of the media has increased phenomenally," he said.
But Camilla Parker Bowles, mistress of Britain's Prince Charles who makes the headlines almost as often as Charles's ex-wife Diana, has no entry.
"Media hype alone won't let you in," said Fitzwilliams. However famous a person, he or she needs to have achieved something of historic importance to be included.

The United States has the most names in "Who's Who", with new entries for 1997 including singer Mariah Carey, golfer Tiger Woods and world boxing champion Evander Holyfield, who temporarily lost a chunk of his ear when opponent Mike Tyson bit it off during a recent fight.
